label: database-row-insert-fresh-table
notes: Supersedes the 2026-07-30 baseline, which was captured against whatever
the catalog happened to hold. That table drifted from 35 rows to 358 as
the measuring itself added rows, so its 192ms median describes a table
size, not a code version, and must not be compared against.
The scenario now creates its own empty v2 database per run. Sample i is
therefore an insert into a table of size i, which is what makes
rowInsertGrowthRatio meaningful: it is the mean of the last quarter of
the samples over the mean of the first.
A growth ratio near 1.0 is the goal. At 1.66 over only 40 rows, the write
is O(rows) — the owner-table projection re-derives every row on every
single-row write. `a3d6ac73` halved the per-row constant; it did not
rowInsertMedianMs is submit -> the first read-back that started after the
write landed. Runs are only comparable at the same iteration count.
